traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 107 Passifloraceae: upright trees and shrubs, or herbaceous climbers with tendrils; leaves alternate, entire or lobed, often with glands on the stalk; stipules usually small and falling; sepals 5, petals 5, rarely none; a corona of threads or scales; ovary superior, often on a stalk, of one cell with 3 (rarely 4 or 5) placentas on its wall; fruit a capsule or a berry (the passion fruit). The regular flower is from common knowledge, inferred.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312, family Passifloraceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral; read as "spiral".

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312, family Passifloraceae: leaf division simple, usually; read as {"simple": "usually"}. The books add compound (rarely): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312: palmately compound.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312, family Passifloraceae: leaf incision lobed (palmately), often; read as {"lobed": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 314, 315, family Passifloraceae: inflorescence cyme (or solitary flower), often; read as {"cyme": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Wikipedia Passifloraceae (read 2026-10-17): ~750 spp, no data on flower sexes. From general knowledge, not a page: Passiflora (~550, bisexual flowers) outnumbers the dioecious Adenia (~100), so hermaphrodite leads. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.leaf_margin.note: DELTA, Passifloraceae (read 2026-10-17): margins entire (no teeth given); Lucid key (read 2026-10-17): entire, crenate or serrate.

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Passifloraceae (read 2026-10-17): ~750 spp in ~27 genera, no genus counts or fruit by genus. Weighting from general knowledge, not a page read: Passiflora (~550 spp, berry) is the large majority against capsular Adenia (~100) and smaller genera.
